lesson_body:
Welcome to Day 3 of our exciting Unit 2 on Shapes and Spaces! Today, we dive deeper into the wonderful world of shapes by exploring the characteristics of two-dimensional shapes and their real-life applications. We will focus on four key shapes: circles, squares, triangles, and rectangles.

To begin our lesson, let's gather in a circle and play a fun game called 'Shape Hunt'. As we walk around the classroom, I will call out a shape. If you see that shape around you, point to it and shout ‘found it!’ For instance, if I say ‘circle,’ look for any item in the room that is circular, like a clock or a plate. This will help us recognize how shapes are everywhere in our environment!

Next, let’s take a closer look at each shape. We will use our shape cards, which have different images of each shape. We will discuss the number of sides and corners each shape has. For example, a triangle has three sides and three corners, while a square has four equal sides and four corners. We’ll use our fingers to count the sides together. This will develop not only your shape recognition but also your counting skills. 

After that, we will create a ‘Shape Collage’. You will use colored paper to cut out each shape. You will have red for circles, blue for squares, yellow for triangles, and green for rectangles. Once you’ve cut your shapes, we will glue them onto a poster board. We will then display our collages around the classroom for everyone to admire! This activity will strengthen your fine motor skills while reinforcing your understanding of shapes.

We will wrap up our lesson by sitting in our circle again and sharing what we learned about our favorite shape and where we find it in our daily lives. Can you think of a round object in your home? How about a square-shaped window? This reflection will help connect our learning to the real world! Remember, shapes aren’t just in your math book; they are all around us, and you’ll start seeing them everywhere you go.
interactive_assignment: For your interactive assignment today, let’s make a Shape Scavenger Hunt! You will be given a worksheet with pictures of the shapes we learned about today: triangles, squares, circles, and rectangles. Your task is to go around the classroom or your home (with a parent’s permission) and find items that match the shapes listed. Draw a picture of each shape you find next to the corresponding shape on your worksheet. If you can’t find an item that matches, use your imagination and draw something that could be that shape! After completing your scavenger hunt, we will share our findings during circle time. This will help everyone practice their shape recognition while having fun exploring!
